speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in. I see you are a 34-year-old male with a history of AIDS presenting with decreased vision and black spots in your right eye. To narrow this down, have you noticed any floaters, flashes of light, or a curtain-like shadow over your vision recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of decreased vision and seeing black spots in the right eye. He reports no pain, and the left eye is asymptomatic. He mentions being treated for fungal esophagitis 6 months ago and was diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma 2 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient has a history of AIDS, fungal esophagitis, and Kaposi's sarcoma, but no pain or flashes of light. Given the black spots and vision loss, have you noticed any new floaters or a sensation like a curtain coming down over your right eye?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Decreased vision and black spots in the right eye. I also have No pain, Left eye is asymptomatic. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: CMV Retinitis

While I acknowledge your previous mention of Tuberculosis, the presence of "black spots" (hemorrhages and necrosis) without pain or floaters in an AIDS patient is clinically classic for Cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis, which requires urgent confirmation. I will now perform a slit-lamp exam and order a fluorescein angiogram to confirm the diagnosis and rule out other posterior segment causes.

REQUEST TEST: Fundoscopy
